manual: I. Basic Experiment Information1. Experiment Title: Dissolution of Crystalline Sugar vs. Amorphous Sugar Glass in Water2. Subject: Healthcare – Pharmacy (Physical Pharmacy)3. Experiment Objective: To visually compare and understand the difference in dissolution behavior between crystalline sugar and amorphous sugar glass in water, and relate the phenomenon to solid-state structure and free energy.II. Experimental EquipmentTwo identical clear glass beakers, room-temperature water, crystalline sugar (granulated sucrose), sugar glass shards (amorphous sucrose), glass stirring rods (2), camera with fixed focus for time-lapse recording.III. Experimental Procedure1. Preparation: Place two identical beakers side by side on a flat surface. Pour equal volumes of room-temperature water into each beaker.2. Material Addition: Add an equal mass of crystalline sugar into the left beaker. Add an equal mass of sugar glass shards into the right beaker.3. Stirring: Gently stir both beakers simultaneously and equally using separate glass rods.4. Recording: Fix the camera focus and record the dissolution process using time-lapse photography.5. Completion: Stop stirring once clear differences in dissolution behavior are observed.IV. Observation of Experimental PhenomenaInitially, both sugars are visible as solid particles. During stirring, sugar glass in the right beaker rapidly disperses and dissolves, causing quick clarification. Crystalline sugar in the left beaker dissolves more slowly, with visible granules persisting for a longer time.V. Summary of Experimental PrincipleSugar glass is an amorphous solid with higher free energy and greater molecular mobility, allowing water to penetrate and dissolve it rapidly. Crystalline sugar has an ordered lattice with lower free energy, requiring more time for water molecules to break intermolecular interactions, resulting in slower dissolution. This demonstrates the influence of solid-state structure on dissolution rate, an important concept in pharmacy.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target Concept: Comparison of dissolution behavior between crystalline and amorphous solids based on solid-state structure and free energy differences. Minimum assumptions include identical solvent conditions, equal solute mass, and equal stirring intensity.Expected Phenomena Storyline: Phase 1 – Two identical beakers with water and distinct sugar forms are presented side by side. Phase 2 – Upon equal stirring, sugar glass rapidly disperses and dissolves, while crystalline sugar remains visible longer. Phase 3 – Over time-lapse progression, the right beaker becomes clear sooner than the left. Visibility Constraints: Fixed camera focus, clear side-by-side framing, and sufficient clarity to distinguish dissolution rates.
